subject: POC MAP: CoreHealth env setup — org seed, API keys, IP allowlist, peering
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@corehealth.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: POC MAP: CoreHealth env setup — org seed, API keys, IP allowlist, peering

Hi Liam / Maya,

Great to connect yesterday — thanks for the time. Per our conversation, below is a compact mutual action plan to get the POC environment live within two weeks so your infra team can run load/latency checks and we can validate feature parity with your internal workflows. I've attached a MAP worksheet (editable) and a simple VPC diagram.

High-level milestones (owners & target dates):
- Org seed & RBAC: CoreHealth to confirm admin list + existing cloud identity mapping (owner: CoreHealth IT) — target: 2026-05-13
- API key provisioning (hosted sandbox): Redwood issues scoped API keys for test tenants (owner: Jordan / Neha) — target: 2026-05-12
- IP allowlist & ephemeral NAT IPs: CoreHealth to provide public egress IPs for allowlist; Redwood to provide test IPs for inbound access (owner: CoreHealth IT / Evelyn) — target: 2026-05-13
- VPC peering / PrivateLink (optional): exchange VPC IDs and routes, schedule peering window (owner: CoreHealth IT / Evelyn) — target: 2026-05-14
- Smoke tests & acceptance criteria: sample throughput + latency checks, model inference sanity tests, auth path validation (owner: CoreHealth & Redwood) — target: 2026-05-15

Notes/Requirements:
- API keys will be scoped to a single test org and rotated after the POC; production keys require contract signature.
- If you prefer VPC peering over IP allowlist, we'll need an outbound CIDR and route table entries; diagram attached shows the minimal route config.
- We recommend creating a dedicated service account in your org for the POC to simplify RBAC and auditability.

Next step: can you confirm the admin list + whether you want peering or allowlist by EOD Wednesday (2026-05-12)? We'll stage the sandbox keys immediately once we have that.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment stubs: MAP_worksheet_CoreHealth_v1.xlsx (xlsx), network_diagram_vpc_peering.png (png)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@corehealth.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Rios <maya.rios@corehealth.ai>, CoreHealth IT <it@corehealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:11:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC MAP: CoreHealth env setup — org seed, API keys, IP allowlist, peering

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear checklist. Quick answers:
- Admin list: myself (liam@corehealth.ai), Maya Rios (maya.rios@corehealth.ai), and our infra lead Cesar Valdez (cesar@corehealth.ai). We'll create a team in our IdP and share SAML metadata if you need it.
- Peering vs allowlist: We'd prefer VPC peering for data plane security, but can fall back to IP allowlist if peering takes longer.
- CIDR: Our staging VPC is 10.40.0.0/16; we can open a peering window Friday 05/14 morning.

A few questions:
1) What is the expected NAT/outbound IP range Redwood will use to call our enforcement APIs? We need that for allowlist fallback.
2) For API key rotation during the POC, can keys be restricted to a single model family and to the test org only?

We'll pull the MAP worksheet into our tracking board and add owners. Sending Cesar into this thread.

— Liam
CTO, CoreHealth
liam@corehealth.ai

On Mon, May 11, 2026 at 09:23 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC MAP: CoreHealth env setup — org seed, API keys, IP allowlist, peering

Hi Liam / team,

Great — thanks for the quick replies. Quick answers inline:
1) Outbound IPs: For the hosted sandbox we have a small ephemeral egress pool. For the peering flow you won't see our NAT egress; for allowlist fallback we can provide the current test egress IP block: 34.210.45.64/28 (subject to change; we'll notify you before the POC window).
2) API key scoping: yes — keys can be scoped by org + model-family tags and limited to read/generate only (no admin). We'll issue keys with an expiry of 14 days for the test; rotation is manual from our console.

Action: Evelyn will prepare a short peering checklist and the route table snippet you'll need. Jordan / Ben will provision the sandbox org and create one scoped API key once we confirm the peering vs allowlist choice.

Planned timeline (updated):
- 05/12: Redwood provisions sandbox org and creates scoped API key (provisioned but held until peering window)
- 05/13: CoreHealth confirms admin IdP mapping + shares SAML metadata
- 05/14 09:00–11:00 PT: Peering window (if chosen) — Evelyn to run; fallback: Redwood updates allowlist with 34.210.45.64/28
- 05/14 afternoon: run smoke tests, share results (latency, success-rate)

I'll also attach a short checklist in the MAP worksheet to make the routing clear.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC MAP: CoreHealth env setup — org seed, API keys, IP allowlist, peering

Team —

Cesar / CoreHealth IT: attached is the minimal peering checklist and a route table snippet you can paste into your cloud console. Key items: exchange account IDs, VPC IDs, and confirm no overlapping CIDRs (you indicated 10.40.0.0/16, our peering target will be 10.60.0.0/16). Please confirm the peering accepts the following:
- Our peering request will appear from account: 9876543210 (Redwood staging)
- VPC id: vpc-0f3b9cstaging (Redwood staging)

If you accept peering Friday morning 05/14 at 09:00 PT we'll complete the route updates and run end-to-end smoke tests by 13:00 PT. If peering is not accepted we'll add the allowlist entry 34.210.45.64/28 and run tests at 14:00 PT.

Post-tests: we'll share a short report with latency percentiles and token throughput plus a checklist for production next steps (SLA addendum, dedicated capacity options).

Ben — flagging renewal/discount cadence once the POC passes.

Evelyn Hart
Onboarding Engineer, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
